rationale.conceptual: Variational Monte Carlo with wave-function optimization is an established but non-trivial method. It involves multiple interacting components (Jastrow factor, Slater determinant, auxiliary Hamiltonians, structure factors), and the domain of strongly correlated electrons demands careful implementation of the model and optimization procedure.
rationale.execution: The reproduction pipeline has several stages: analytic atomic-limit derivation, large-U VMC scan for phase boundaries, structure-factor extraction, and a small-U VMC run for the charge-ordered metal. This multi-stage pipeline with dependencies is moderately complex, but relies only on standard libraries (numpy, scipy) and moderate scripting.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces a VMC study with Jastrow-Slater wave functions for a two-orbital Hubbard model, requiring implementation of a non-trivial algorithm, but no deep GPU needs. It is a moderate conceptual and execution challenge.

compute_estimate.reasoning: VMC on finite clusters (L up to ~10) is CPU-bound, not GPU-accelerated; memory is modest to hold the lattice and wave-function parameters, no large external datasets.
